Risk to people: The recording picks up more than the consultation needs: a relative, a phone call, a side comment.
Measures: Dr. A starts and stops it. Stops before the examination. Visit types excluded. A third person must also agree, or Dr. A does not record.

Risk to people: Audio or transcripts at the provider are seen by someone who should not: breach or misuse by an employee.
Measures: Art. 28 agreement. Encryption at rest and in transit. Access limited. Audio deleted within 24 hours and text within 72 hours. Security evidence checked before the pilot (C1).

Risk to people: A mistake in the transcript or draft (a drug, a dose, the wrong side) enters the record and affects care.
Measures: A draft is never filed unread. Dr. A checks names, doses and sides. No direct link to the record. Pilot stops after two errors that reach the record.

Risk to people: The provider or a sub-processor uses the data to train or improve its models, or for its own purposes.
Measures: Contract bans it. Setting checked and noted. Sub-processors listed, and changes notified.

Risk to people: Data reaches a country outside the EU through a sub-processor or through support access.
Measures: EU region and EU-only support in the contract. Sub-processor list. A transfer assessment if any location is outside the EU (C1).

Risk to people: Patients feel they cannot refuse, and hold back information or avoid care.
Measures: Ask each time, in a standard sentence. Refusal has no consequence. A sign, and a notice that says so.

Risk to people: The tablet or the account is lost or taken, with audio or notes on it.
Measures: Nothing stored on the tablet. Screen lock, device encryption, remote wipe, two-step verification on the account.

Risk to people: The transcripts are used for other purposes: checking staff, marketing, research.
Measures: Purpose fixed in the notice and the contract. Only Dr. A has access. A new purpose needs a new DPIA.

Risk to people: A patient cannot get access to, correct or have deleted what the provider holds.
Measures: Audio and text are gone within 72 hours. The final note is in the record, with the rights procedure. The provider must support deletion on request.
